label: Paul (Saul of Tarsus)

label: Porcius Festus (procurator of Judaea)
dates: procurator of Judaea after Felix; the date is disputed, most scholars 58-60
note: Named by Josephus as sent by Nero as Felix's successor (Ant. 20.182); his prutah coinage is dated year 5 of Nero (58/59).

label: Antonius Felix (procurator of Judea, c. 52-59 CE)
note: Brother of the freedman Pallas; Claudius 'sent Felix, the brother of Pallas, to take care of the affairs of Judea' (Josephus, Ant. 20.137); Tacitus, Hist. 5.9: he 'exercised the power of a king in the spirit of a slave'; Annals 12.54: he thought 'he could do any evil act with impunity'; recalled and nearly punished, saved by his brother Pallas (Ant. 20.182-184).

label: Herod Agrippa II
aka: Agrippa II; Marcus Julius Agrippa; 'King Agrippa' of Acts 25-26
dates: 27/28 - c. 92/100 CE; tetrarch of Chalcis 48-53, king 53 - c. 92/100

label: Acts 26:1
text: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.

label: Acts 26:2
text: “I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things that I am accused by the Jews,

label: Acts 26:3
text: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.

label: Acts 26:4
text: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;

label: Acts 26:5
text: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

label: Acts 26:6
text: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,

label: Acts 26:7
text: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!

label: Acts 26:8
text: Why is it judged incredible with you, if God does raise the dead?

label: Acts 26:9
text: “I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

label: Acts 26:10
text: This I also did in Jerusalem. I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.

label: Acts 26:11
text: Punishing them often in all the synagogues, I tried to make them blaspheme. Being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.

label: Acts 26:12
text: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,

label: Acts 26:13
text: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.

label: Acts 26:14
text: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’

label: Acts 26:15
text: “I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ “He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

label: Acts 26:16
text: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen, and of the things which I will reveal to you;

label: Acts 26:17
text: delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,

label: Acts 26:18
text: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’

label: Acts 26:19
text: “Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,

label: Acts 26:20
text: but declared first to them of Damascus, at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

label: Acts 26:21
text: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple, and tried to kill me.

label: Acts 26:22
text: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen,

label: Acts 26:23
text: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to these people and to the Gentiles.”

label: Acts 26:24
text: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!”

label: Acts 26:25
text: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.

label: Acts 26:26
text: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.

label: Acts 26:27
text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”

label: Acts 26:28
text: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”

label: Acts 26:29
text: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”

label: Acts 26:30
text: The king rose up with the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them.

label: Acts 26:31
text: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”

label: Acts 26:32
text: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

label: Paul made his defense before King Agrippa, 'expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews'
statement: Paul thought himself happy to make his defense before King Agrippa concerning all the accusations of the Jews, especially because Agrippa was expert (gnosten) in all the customs and questions among the Jews.

label: Paul had lived as a Pharisee, 'after the strictest sect of our religion'
statement: Paul says all the Jews had known from the first that, if they were willing to testify, he had lived a Pharisee according to the strictest sect (akribeistaten hairesin) of the Jewish religion.

label: Paul was judged for the hope of the promise - that God raises the dead, the hope of the twelve tribes
statement: Paul stood to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to the fathers, which the twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hoped to attain: 'Why is it judged incredible with you, if God does raise the dead?' - the Pharisaic hope of resurrection.

label: Paul, with authority from the chief priests, imprisoned the saints, gave his vote against them when put to death, and persecuted them to foreign cities
statement: Paul thought he ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth: he shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, gave his vote (kateneika psēphon) against them when they were put to death, punished them often in all the synagogues trying to make them blaspheme, and persecuted them even to foreign cities.
note: Whether Paul was a formally voting member of the Sanhedrin is debated (the brief grades this D). No fetched page stating the debate was found this run, so the dispute is recorded in the note only, not as a graded edge (not-claimed; needs reviewer judgment).

label: At noon on the Damascus road a light brighter than the sun shone around Paul and his companions; a voice spoke in the Hebrew language
statement: As Paul traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests, at noon he saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around him and those who traveled with him; when they had all fallen to the earth he heard a voice saying in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?' (Miracle/vision claim; searched, no external evidence found.)

label: 'It is hard for you to kick against the goads' repeats a known Greek proverb
statement: The risen Jesus' words to Saul, 'It is hard for you to kick against the goads' (pros kentra laktizein), repeat a Greek proverb for resisting a superior power, known from Euripides, Bacchae 794-795.
note: The proverb appears only in the Acts 26 retelling; it is not found in Acts 9:4 or 22:7 (fetched Wikipedia 'Acts 26' article says so explicitly).

label: The voice appointed Paul a servant and witness, to deliver him from the people and the Gentiles and send him to open their eyes
statement: The voice said, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting', and appointed Paul a servant and witness of what he had seen and of what would be revealed to him, delivering him from the people and from the Gentiles and sending him to open their eyes, to turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins. (Vision claim; searched, no external evidence found.)

label: Paul was not disobedient to the heavenly vision but declared repentance in Damascus, Jerusalem, Judea and to the Gentiles
statement: Paul was not disobedient to the heavenly vision, but declared first to those at Damascus, at Jerusalem, throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

label: The Jews seized Paul in the temple and tried to kill him
statement: For this reason (his preaching to the Gentiles) the Jews seized Paul in the temple and tried to kill him.

label: Paul testified to small and great, saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen - the Christ must suffer and, first by resurrection, proclaim light
statement: Having obtained help from God, Paul stood testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles.

label: Festus said with a loud voice: 'Paul, you are mad; your great learning is driving you insane'
statement: As Paul made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, 'Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!'

label: Paul: 'I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but speak words of truth'; the king knows of these things, for none of it was hidden from him
statement: Paul answered that he was not mad but spoke words of truth and reasonableness; the king knows of these things, to whom Paul spoke freely, persuaded that none of them was hidden from him, 'for this has not been done in a corner', and he asked whether King Agrippa believed the prophets.

label: 'This has not been done in a corner' - a Greek idiom for what is public
statement: Paul's words 'this has not been done in a corner' (ou gar estin en gonia pepragmenon) use a Greek idiom contrasting corner-seclusion with public notoriety.

label: The name 'Christian' (Christianos) was current for the movement's adherents in Agrippa's time
statement: Agrippa answered, 'With a little persuasion (en oligō) are you trying to make me a Christian?' - the name Christianos was current enough by c. 59/60 CE for a Herodian king to use it in irony.

label: The king, the governor, Bernice and those sitting with them withdrew and agreed Paul did nothing worthy of death or bonds
statement: The king rose up with the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them; when they had withdrawn they spoke to one another, saying, 'This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.'

label: Agrippa told Festus the man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar
statement: Agrippa said to Festus, 'This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.'
